subject: INTD
title: Introduction to International Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: An interdisciplinary introduction to the field of International Development Studies focusing on the theory and practice of development. It examines various approaches to international development, including past and present relationships between developed and underdeveloped societies, and pays particular attention to power and resource distribution globally and within nations.

subject: INTD
title: History of Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: A history of development, focusing on the ideologies as well as the practices that have shaped how empires, governments, corporations, and individuals have sought to 'improve' the world—most often, but not exclusively, in the global south. Themes will include colonialism, gender, race, economic growth, poverty, geopolitics, multilateralism, foreign aid, south-south relations, philanthropy, and the environment.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken INTD 397, when topic was "History of Development" in Winter 2024.

subject: INTD
title: Culture and Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: This is a general survey course intended to familiarize students with the complexities surrounding the interaction between culture and development from a variety of theoretical perspectives. Specific themes may include religion, democracy, gender, diaspora communities and the environment, using relevant case studies from the developing world.

prerequisites.text: A 200 or 300 level course related to International Development, or permission of instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken INTD 397 with the same topic: "Culture and Development" prior to Fall 2017. Open to U2 and U3 students only.

subject: INTD
title: Disasters and Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: Examines how disasters shape and are shaped by socio-economic conditions, inequalities and development processes through interdisciplinary investigation and a wide range of case studies. Analyzes disaster risk reduction, response and recovery efforts from the global to local levels, as well as survivors’ perspectives and experiences.

prerequisites.text: A 200 or 300 level course related to International Development, or permission of instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken INTD 397 when topic was "Disasters and Development" [fall 2018]. Opento U2 and U3 students only.

subject: INTD
title: Civil Society and Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: Introduction to the study of civil society and development. Critically engages with both conventional socio-political views and emerging perspectives of civil society. Employs political, sociological, and anthropological perspectives to understand the multifaceted, and socio-cultural implications of civil society in both developing and developed countries. Examines civil society’s impact, capacity, and behavior through a wide range of development themes.

prerequisites.text: A 200 or 300 level course related to International Development, or permission of instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken INTD 397 when topic was "Civil Society and Development" [Winter 2017, Winter 2018]. Open to U2 and U3 students only.

subject: INTD
title: Quantitative Methods for Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: Introduction to quantitative methods for impact evaluation. Builds from fundamental concepts in statistics; introduction of an intuitive conceptual framework to think about causal effects. Simple but rigorous data analytics, design and implement randomized controlled trials, regression analysis, or implement other main methods for impact evaluation.

subject: INTD
title: Ethnographic Approaches to Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: Consideration of how anthropologists have used ethnographic methods to evaluate, criticize and reform development. Drawing on ethnographies of “Big D” development, as well as small-scale grassroots initiatives, exploration of how qualitative methods have been used to strengthen development practice from within and deconstruct development ideology from without. Topics include state driven, participatory and internationally sponsored development; gender; “aidnography”; neoliberalism; markets and microcredit.

subject: INTD
title: Environmental Challenges in Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: Examination of some of the great environmental challenges of our times, and some of the ways in which the development community has tackled them.

subject: INTD
title: Political Ecologies of Development
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: Examination of the environmental dimensions of development through the interdisciplinary framework of political ecology. Introduction to how power, inequality, governance, and economic interests shape human-environmental relations across local, national, and global scales. The theoretical foundations of political ecology and applying them to key development challenges such as resource extraction, land and water governance, conservation, urban pollution, and climate change. Critical examination of environmental problems as social and political processes.

prerequisites.text: A 200 or 300 level course related to International Development, or permission of the instructor.

subject: INTD
title: Climate Change, Culture and Power
offeredBy: Inst for the St of Development
description: Examination of climate change as a cultural, political, andhistorical process. Drawing on anthropology, history, political economy, and environmental studies, it explores how climate change is understood, governed, and debated across different societies and scales. The relationships between environmental change, economic systems, political institutions, and social inequalities, as well as the ways climate futures are imagined and contested. Situating climate change within broader debates in international development and global environmental governance.

prerequisites.text: A 200 or 300 level course related to International Development, or permission of the instructor.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken INTD 498 when the topic was "Climate Change, Culture and Power" in Fall 2025.
